transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman, Tennessee failed to kill a condemned
inmate last night.
Christa Pike was given a lethal injection two separate times.
She survived both and was then moved to a hospital.
Pike's lawyers say she was clearly alive and snoring after Tennessee's second botched
execution this year.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has halted the state's remaining execution schedule this
year.
Military officials say the incident yesterday aboard a fly Dubai passenger plane was an
attempted terror attack.
Passengers helped subdue a copilot who allegedly attacked the pilot and then apparently tried
to crash the plane.
And Bier's Kat Lonsdorf reports from Tel Aviv there's little information known about a motive.
Both the pilot and the copilot are alive.
They're being interviewed by investigators in Saudi Arabia.
The UAE has also opened an investigation and Netanyahu has said Israel will be involved.
The pilot who was stabbed is from India.
Both Netanyahu and India's prime minister have commended him.
And the copilot who did the attacking is from Oman.
It's still unclear if he was acting alone.
And Bier's Kat Lonsdorf reporting.
One of Iraq's most powerful militias backed by Iran says it will stop its attacks.
And Bier's Jane Arap reports from Baghdad the U.S. military withdrew from Iraq yesterday.
Qatab Hezbollah said in a statement that the Islamic resistance had won this round against
what it called the U.S. occupation.
The U.S. on Wednesday announced it had withdrawn its military forces and closed the headquarters
here of an anti-ISIS coalition it has led since 2014.
The Islamic resistance is a grouping of Iran-backed militias that have frequently claimed attacks
against U.S. targets in Iraq.
Qatab Hezbollah directed its fighters to stop all attacks apart from targeting aircraft
violating Iraqi airspace.
Jane Araphe and Pierre News Baghdad.
President Trump will hold a campaign event later today south of Oklahoma City.
He's working to boost support among the Republican Party faithful.
And Pierre's Deepa Shabiram reports Trump attended a Hispanic heritage celebration yesterday.
Trump told supporters at the White House, even if they don't love their Republican candidate,
the alternative would be worse.
Even if you don't like somebody so much, it doesn't matter, it's a vote for good things.
You know, it's hard to explain that, but you may not love your Congressperson, your Senate,
but it's a road like in Michigan, are you going to vote for a guy who's a communist?
That was a day get Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El Sayed, who's in his party's
left flank, but is not a communist or a Democratic socialist.
Trump plans to campaign in Texas this week and has said he'll also make stops in Iowa
and Alaska later on.
Deepa Shabiram, NPR News, the White House.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The Senate has confirmed acting Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling to the position.
Sonderling has run the agency since former Labor Secretary Laurie Chavez de Rheemer left.
She had been accused of abusing her office.
A Senate committee has advanced the nomination of Dr. Nicole Safire to be the next U.S. Surgeon
General.
It is not clear when the Senate will take up her nomination.
The Trump administration has made some last minute changes to the forms used by U.S. citizens
who cast ballots from outside the country.
Now voting advocates are raising concerns.
And Pierre's Hansi Lo Wang reports the changes come as Republicans continue their push to
block some overseas U.S. citizens from voting.
Many overseas and military voters use two absentee voting forms that are overseen by
the Pentagon.
In August, the Trump administration made an emergency request to remove a long-standing
category for U.S. citizens who were born abroad and have never lived in the United States.
And sometimes because their U.S. citizen parents or legal guardians served overseas in the
U.S. military.
Many states allow these citizens to vote if a parent last lived or was registered to vote
there before leaving the country.
The Pentagon says it now believes those overseas citizens are not eligible to use its forms.
But that state election officials can continue processing older versions of the forms.
The change comes after the Republican National Committee sued more than a half a dozen states
for allowing these U.S. citizens to vote.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
SpaceX has scheduled a Florida launch later this morning of its Crew 13 mission.
The four-person crew is scheduled to spend six months in orbit at the International Space
Station.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Tennessee failed to execute condemned inmate Christa Pike after two botched lethal injections
Copilot attacked pilot aboard fly Dubai passenger plane in apparent attempted terror attack
Iran-backed Iraqi militia Qatab Hezbollah says it will stop attacks on US targets
US military withdrew from Iraq and closed anti-ISIS coalition headquarters after 2014
President Trump campaigns in Oklahoma to boost support among Republican Party faithful
Senate confirms Keith Sonderling as Labor Secretary after Laurie Chavez de Rheemer's departure
Senate committee advances Dr. Nicole Safire nomination to be next US Surgeon General
Trump administration removes citizenship category from overseas voting forms, raising concerns
Republican National Committee sued states allowing certain overseas US citizens to vote
SpaceX scheduled to launch Crew 13 mission to International Space Station from Florida
